result.judge_notes: pass 1 (A=without, B=with): Both answers recommend a single bar chart with accurate counts and point out that ride time is not the same as lateness. A's caption is ready to publish as written, and its 4-band regrouping (110/211/50/9) is correct and easy for parents to read; its only slip is saying 'more than 40' where the data means 40 or more. B keeps finer bins, which show the spread better, but its color scheme and caption depend on bracketed placeholders for a schedule the user doesn't have, and its headline band ('15–25') sits awkwardly beside its own '20–24 most common' line. | pass 2 (A=with, B=without): Both answers recommend one plain bar chart, flag that ride time is not the same as lateness, and get the key figures right (59 of 380 at 30+ minutes, 9 trips at 40+). A keeps more detail and describes the build precisely: it merges only the last two bins, puts counts on the bars, colours bars past the posted time, and its caption is accurate throughout. B's four bands are readable, but its caption says '2 of every 100 took more than 40' when the 9 trips are 40 or more, and it adds an estimated median of '22 minutes', which brings in imprecision.
